egress.terms: Claimed free. The business page is titled «Eliminate Egress Fees» and argues against providers «that charge hidden egress fees», and the pricing JSON-LD implies flat-rate. But no numbered egress allowance, no fair-use clause and no overage rate is published anywhere on the site. So the claim cannot be falsified from outside.

tooling: None documented. No public API, no WebDAV, no S3 endpoint, no rclone backend, no CLI. The product page describes «Zero-Knowledge Personal Vault», AES-256-GCM client-side encryption, mobile sync and a web UI. This is the disqualifying gap.
chaining: Per-account consumer plans; no documented route that uses several accounts and no API to automate one.
limits_note: Zero programmatic API access. Client-side zero-knowledge encryption ensures that stored data is encrypted prior to transmission. Marketing comparison pages advertise promotional pricing while direct pricing endpoints returned incomplete placeholder pages on 2026-10-21.

extras.limits_verbatim: Zero programmatic access. Client-side zero-knowledge encryption means even a reverse-engineered API would return ciphertext only to the holder of the key, which is fine for backup but blocks the CDN/serving workload entirely. The entire site is SEO-shaped: multiple near-identical 2026 comparison articles on its own domain ranking itself #1, with an «Independent Industry Audit» framing. The 1 TB price is also contradicted by its own pricing page rendering an empty shell to every reader that reached it — /pricing, /pricing.html and /cloud-storage-pricing all resolved to the same 37-word stub with `confidence: low`.

extras.agent_focus: Wave 7 cheap-PAID lane, regional angle: storage sold in RUB / CNY / BRL / INR / ZAR / TRY / PLN / UAH that never appears on Western price lists. Every paid candidate carries price_per_tb_month at USD-converted list price. FX fixed 2026-10-21 from open.er-api.com: RUB 82.5719/USD, CNY 6.6913, BRL 5.0231, INR 94.9952, ZAR 16.3972, TRY 49.5978, PLN 3.8923, UAH 45.0922, EUR 0.89075/USD. Excluded per brief: AWS, Azure, GCP, Alibaba Cloud, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, IDrive e2. Headline result: the true regional floor with genuinely free egress is ~$2.00/TB/mo (Yandex 360 Profi 3 TB on a Russian card) rising to ~$4.17/TB/mo for the same product bought with a foreign card, and ~$5.95-7.56/TB/mo for flat-rate Western-facing file storage (TheHost, Rollin Host). Everything advertised below ~$2/TB/mo in this set is either capacity-capped, egress-metered, or unverifiable marketing.
